title: Intuition that complex results need complex plans comes from engineering

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Intuition that complex results need complex plans comes from engineering

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The intuition that complex objects require complex construction plans fails because it derives from engineering, where designers restrict themselves to systems whose behavior they can understand and predict, a constraint nature does not share.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Yet to do this reliably, we have to restrict ourselves to systems whose behavior we can readily understand and predict—for unless we can foresee how a system will behave, we cannot be sure that the system will do what we want.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “The Need for a New Intuition” (from p. 39), p. 40. Scope: human intuition about complexity and the practice of engineering

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.19

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Current surveys and design corpora could test restricted associations, but no existing dataset cleanly identifies the claimed causal origin of human intuition. The contrast with nature is too broad to adjudicate as one empirical proposition.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Survey engineering designs and practitioners to measure preferences for predictable systems, and experimentally test whether engineering exposure predicts belief that complex outcomes need complex plans. Compare this account with alternative cognitive explanations.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Failure of the intuition is partly a conceptual conclusion.

Engineering practice and nature are heterogeneous.

The historical origin of an intuition is difficult to infer from current behavior.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.1
analysis feasibility: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.2
discriminating power: 0.15
data existence: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The sentence is a diagnosis of why a piece of common sense fails. Engineering artifacts and natural forms can be described, and that description does not identify the psychological source of the intuition or show that the diagnosis is the reason the intuition fails. The claim has no separating measurement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim explains a habit of thought by its origin in engineering practice. A survey of design methods can describe what engineers build; it cannot show that this origin is why the intuition fails, nor measure the intuition itself.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The source of an intuition is not an observable with a refuting outcome.

Several historical origins are compatible with the same engineering record.
